text:
Ethan: Opening thread for Tidewell Labs onprem peering postmortem follow-up. Isolation root cause: appliance dropped fragmented packets after model shard traffic increased; PMTU blackhole + TCP MSS not clamped. Need owners and hard due dates.
Rhea: Oof. Can we categorize into immediate mitigation vs infra fixes?
Ethan: Immediate: apply TCP MSS clamp on Tidewell edge and disable LRO/GRO on the interface. Infra fixes: BFD + adjacency health probe, small eBGP policy change to prefer symmetric path, and a synthetic traffic detector.
Ming: I can do the immediate network side changes. ETA tomorrow morning. I'll create runbook.
Priya: I'll own the synthetic detector (agent that injects tiny TCP flows to validate fragmentation). 5 business days to ship.
OpsCoord: I'll coordinate the maintenance window with Tidewell ops and gather access method.
Ethan: Please post ticket numbers here and include rollback plans. Also note recurring pattern: similar flaps matched to large model refreshes (approx every 45 days) — add recurring review to prevent regressions.
Ming: Ticket: TW-9001 for immediate TCP MSS clamp + NIC offload toggles. Runbook snippet:
```steps:
1) verify current PMTU with tracepath to each peering IP
2) set iptables TCPMSS clamp to 1400 on peer-facing veth
3) disable LRO/GRO on interface: ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off
4) restart peering daemon
5) run small shard-transfer test and monitor 5min for retransmits```
Priya: Ticket: TW-9002 for synthetic detector. Detector will alert on >1% packet reassembly failures or >200ms median RTT for synthetic TCP probe over 3m.
Ethan: Ticket: TW-9003 for adjacency healthchecks + routing preference change; rollout plan: canary 6 hosts for 24h, then 30% for 72h. Rollback: restore previous policy and remove BFD timers.
OnCall-Bot: Reminder: Incident doc created https://redwood.internal/incidents/TW-3031/postmortem (owner: Ethan).
Rhea: Add validation step in runbook to query inference proxy KV cache warmup and model shard success rate. We saw cache misses spike during the outage.
Ming: Good point, adding: post-change validate KV hitrate and model shard handshake times (<150ms).
OpsCoord: I've scheduled a 45m sync with Tidewell for 2026-04-06 09:30 PST to approve maintenance, sent invites.
Priya: Also adding unit test to our detector CI to simulate PMTU blackhole + fragment drop; this should prevent silent regressions.
Ethan: Action tracker summary (please paste into ticket comments):
- TW-9001 (Ming) TCP MSS clamp + NIC offload toggles 1 due 2026-04-02
- TW-9002 (Priya) synthetic detector + CI unit test 1 due 2026-04-09
- TW-9003 (Ethan) adjacency healthchecks & routing pref change 1 due 2026-04-23 (canary first)
- Tidewell maintenance sign-off (OpsCoord) 1 meeting 2026-04-06
- Recurring review: peering-regression postmortem every quarter (owner: Rhea)
Ming: Quick question 1 do we have shared SSH/jumpbox for their edge? I need cert access for the window.
OpsCoord: Tidewell provided a bastion with cert auth; I'll DM creds to Ming after sign-off.
Priya: FYI I'll instrument extra telemetry to capture IP fragment stats and correlate with model shard traffic.
Rhea: We should also add a small guardrail in the deployment pipeline to throttle shard redistribution if end-to-end path shows elevated fragment drops.
Ethan: Agreed. Please update TW tickets before EOD tomorrow and mark any external blockers. We'll reconvene after the Tidewell sync. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
